remaining_questions.question: First letter, ח or ה? Even in the full-height crop and band3, the glyph looks open at the upper left, much like the ה of בָּהֶם beside it. Compare the closed ח of חִלַּפְתָּם on the same line. The English 'no delight' and the sense support חֵפֶץ, so the candidate is left unchanged. If a human can see an open ה on the print at higher magnification, should it be encoded as a printed sic (הֵפֶץ, corr חֵפֶץ)?

verdict: I compared all 24 Hebrew text lines of s286 against the new full-height crops and the four overlapping bands, plus the full English s287 page. All vowels, dagesh, meteg, maqaf and full/defective spellings match the candidate. No lower vowel was blocked, and no patches are needed. Human420 (קֲחְתָּה) and Human421 (חַקְתָּה) are applied correctly. The old חוֹשֵׁב doubt was caused by the clipped crop and is now settled as ח. One question about a letter, not a vowel, is still open: the first letter of חֵפֶץ, which may be ח or ה. Because of that, the pointing is approved but the whole source is not.
